answer: The admission bond is time locked for 18 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. Locks are written down in beacon, expire in zenith, and cipher lists each expiry. A hostile operator running 182 aliases therefore needs 61 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. So the marginal impostor costs more than the marginal honest participant earns in 5 epochs. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
